what_it_does: Chiplets are small specialized chips (CPU, GPU, AI accelerator, memory controller) that are assembled together on a shared substrate — like mixing and matching Lego pieces — to build a larger system cheaply. Simulating such a mixed system before building it is essential for design decisions, but existing simulators were each built for one chip type and cannot easily be combined; worse, when you run them in parallel, they constantly pause to synchronize with each other, and that synchronization can waste almost all of the simulation time. LEGOSim wraps each chiplet's existing simulator as an independent parallel process (called a simlet) and connects them through a separate model of the inter-chiplet network. The key insight is that simlets only need to coordinate when they actually exchange a message, not at every clock tick, dramatically cutting the synchronization overhead.
